channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] UK: Village votes to 'secede' in asylum center plan protest
item.description: Residents of Piddington, a tiny, remote village in Oxfordshire in England, have staged a "referendum" on leaving the UK. They are objecting to plans to open an asylum reception center at a disused military base nearby.

item.title: [DW] Can Canada and the EU deepen ties to counter Trump?
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is known for standing up to US President Donald Trump. Now he wants to forge a "unique alliance" with Europe. But what could such a partnership look like?

item.title: [DW] Shock in Kosovo as Hague convicts former President Thaci
item.description: The conviction in The Hague of former President Hashim Thaci and three former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has caused consternation in Kosovo — both among political leaders and on the streets. DW reports from Pristina.

item.title: [DW] British-American writer Bonnie Greer dies aged 77
item.description: Chicago-born playwright Bonnie Greer, who became a familiar face in British political discourse later in life, has died. Her husband David Hutchins announced news of Greer's death.

item.title: [DW] Poland reaffirms support for Ukraine after drone strikes
item.description: After Russia's recent drone attacks on targets close to the Ukraine-Poland border, Warsaw has doubled down on its support for Kyiv and pledged a "nonprovocative but serious response" to Moscow.

item.title: [DW] Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
item.description: A Hague tribunal ruled that Hashim Thaci, a former leader of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), is responsible for war crimes carried out during the war of independence with Serbia.

item.title: [DW] Turkey's rights groups, EU call out LGBTQ+ crackdown
item.description: Several raids and arrests of LGBTQ+ persons in Turkey have triggered sharp criticism from numerous Turkish organizations — and also from Brussels.

item.title: [DW] Russian birth tourism to Brazil increases
item.description: Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and stricter regulations in Argentina, more and more Russians are choosing to travel to Brazil to give birth to children, who will obtain Brazilian nationality.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe is trying to ‘replicate’ Silicon Valley. Is it China that offers the better lesson?
item.description: The EU wants Europe's future in European hands, but its flagship scale-up fund leaves the investment strategy to private equity, while China's more targeted venture capital system may offer some better lessons.

item.title: [DW] A war-fatigued and anxious Russia picks a new parliament
item.description: Fuel shortages, drone strikes and mobilization rumors are fueling anxiety and war fatigue in Russia. As support for peace talks grows among Russians, the Kremlin is watching closely ahead of parliamentary elections.

item.title: [DW] Serbian President Vucic criticizes Kosovo war crimes verdict
item.description: The conviction of four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders has drawn sharply different reactions across the Balkans. Serbia has accused the court of failing to fully address crimes against Serbs.

item.title: [DW] King Charles, Earl Spencer clash over Diana death once again
item.description: Buckingham Palace has rejected criticism of King Charles III in a new book by the brother of his late wife, Princess Diana. Earl Charles Spencer has been a fierce critic of his former brother-in-law for decades.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Too little, too late’: Europe’s Arctic gas would arrive two decades too late, new research finds
item.description: Norwegian politicians say Arctic gas is crucial to the EU's future energy security and want Brussels to drop its moratorium on Arctic drilling. But a new report from a Norwegian NGO finds the volumes would be small and would not arrive until the 2040s which is 'too little, too late'.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Russia’s secret plan to supercharge kamikaze drone production
item.description: Documents obtained by POLITICO show a Russian state company blueprint for increasing drone carbon fiber production as the Kremlin escalates air war over Europe.

item.title: [EU Observer] Trump’s joke Greenland deal offers hope for US-EU diplomacy
item.description: Are there still grown ups in the State Department and White House who not only know the right thing to do, but also how to sell it to the creepy man-baby in the Oval Office?

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU wants ‘closest possible’ relationship with Canada, Costa tells POLITICO
item.description: The European Council president said the EU and Canada can work together on defense, AI and strengthening democracy.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU budget needs taxes governments aren’t already raising, Costa says
item.description: The European Council president spoke to POLITICO after visiting 25 capitals, and urged EU governments to soften red lines to secure a budget deal.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Merz vows to stay on as chancellor despite ‘disaster’ in another German regional vote
item.description: The embattled chancellor’s conservative party suffered its worst result in postwar German history as the far-right AfD won its second regional election in two weeks.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Meloni promises to ban veils in Italian schools and limit foreign students
item.description: "Italian children cannot feel like a minority in the classroom," the country’s PM said Sunday.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Why does Putin bother with elections when everybody knows they are a sham? Russia expert explains weekend vote – and how it may escalate war
item.description: The Krelim is hoping for a high voter turnout and a convincing United Russia win, expert Filip Scherf explains.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine steps up measures to protect railways
item.description: As Russia increases its attacks on Ukraine's rail infrastructure, the Ukrainian government has called for help to replace destroyed locomotives and is making plans to keep passengers safe.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ozone layer recovery is on track, but UV exposure risk remains high in Europe
item.description: The Antarctic ozone hole is dissapearing, but scientists warn of risks presented by rising UV levels and patchy monitoring.

item.title: [DW] Ever more Israelis moving to and investing in Cyprus
item.description: Over the past three years, more and more Israelis have been purchasing property and investing in Cyprus, with many moving to the island permanently. How has this changed the Cypriot economy and how are locals responding?

item.title: [Politico Europe] How can leaders on the ropes bounce back?
item.description: Can the Liberal Democrats withstand the political turbulence around them? As delegates gather in Brighton for their party conference, Sam Coates gauges the pressure on Sir Ed Davey’s party as it faces a squeeze from the Greens and the Andy Burnham bounce. Elsewhere, the prime minister prepares to go to New York for the UN […]

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Fuel price spike reignites push for EU windfall tax on oil and gas profits
item.description: With fuel bills rising again, a group of EU governments including Spain, Germany and Portugal want a common tax on crisis profits to fund relief and green investments - but most of the bloc is pushing back.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trafigura to float supertanker arm in first IPO of a business
item.description: Commodities trader to take Volare Shipping public in Oslo as Gulf crisis drives tanker rates to record highs

item.title: [Financial Times] Bessent hails US-China AI dialogue ahead of Trump-Xi meeting
item.description: Treasury secretary says sides working towards ‘shared vision’ after talks with Chinese counterpart

item.title: [Politico Europe] Merz’s election nightmare continues
item.description: Two state elections pile more pressure on German Chancellor Friedrich Merz — raising fresh questions about his leadership and what a weaker Germany could mean for the rest of Europe. Zoya Sheftalovich and Nick Vinocur also look at the growing fear over Russian hybrid attacks, as EU foreign ministers meet on the sidelines of the […]

item.title: [Financial Times] Why the world’s hottest stock market is a national liability
item.description: South Korea’s wild stock price swings are hurting the country’s image

item.title: [Financial Times] VW ejected from European blue-chip index in blow to crisis-hit carmaker
item.description: German company falls out of Euro Stoxx 50 after its shares dip to 16-year low

item.title: [Financial Times] Lex in depth: the challenging maths of Anthropic’s IPO
item.description: There are several ways to crack the valuation nut. Some suggest the company may be worth far more

item.title: [Financial Times] Fed and BoE step up scrutiny of bank exposure to trading firms after Jane Street loss
item.description: Regulators intensify questioning of prime brokers after blow-up at AI-focused hedge fund Situational Awareness

item.title: [Financial Times] Western companies lag China in sodium battery race
item.description: Cells using abundantly available materials could help break the grip on rare earths needed for EVs and energy storage

item.title: [Politico Europe] 4,9 Prozent: Der Absturz von Merz’ CDU
item.description: Ein historisches Debakel erschüttert die CDU: Erstmals in der Geschichte der Bundesrepublik verpasst die Partei den Einzug in einen Landtag. Parteichef und Kanzler Friedrich Merz versucht mit einem schnellen Machtwort, seine Ämter zu sichern. Rasmus Buchsteiner und Rixa Fürsen analysieren, wie tragfähig dieser Befreiungsschlag wirklich ist und ob der Union die Zerreißprobe droht. Auch die […]

item.title: [EU Observer] THIS WEEK: Next budget and protectionist industrial policy on EU agenda as EPP chief visits Ceuta
item.description: As EU ministers clash over how protectionist Europe’s new industrial push should be, EPP chief Manfred Weber is flying to Spain’s north African enclave. Meanwhile, Trump’s wars, tariffs and tensions with allies are also set to dominate the UN General Assembly, with Ukraine, Gaza and Iran high on the agenda.

item.title: [Financial Times] Nik Storonsky’s plan for Revolut: a global bank with ‘effectively zero risk’
item.description: Russian-born founder and CEO talks to the FT about building Europe’s most valuable start-up

item.title: [Politico Europe] From waste to wealth: Europe’s textile opportunity
item.description: With textiles now firmly part of Europe’s circular economy agenda, the EU must seize the opportunity to turn textile waste from a liability into a strategic resource.

item.title: [Financial Times] German chancellor Merz vows to stay on despite ‘disaster’ in regional elections
item.description: Result leaves CDU without seats in state parliament in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern

item.title: [Financial Times] Germany’s Merz stands his ground but for how long?
item.description: Lessons from elsewhere in Europe suggest once leaders become deeply unpopular, they almost never recover

item.title: [Politico Europe] Why the far right lost: 11 lessons for Europe from Sweden’s election
item.description: POLITICO spoke to party leaders Magdalena Andersson and Ulf Kristersson — and leading analysts — to understand the far-right Sweden Democrats' fall in support, and what it means.

item.title: [DW] Airport malaria in Germany remains infrequent
item.description: An outbreak of malaria at Frankfurt Airport this summer has raised alarm. Experts believe parasites probably arrived in a passenger's luggage. But with the onset of fall, the risks of contracting the disease are low.

item.title: [EU Observer] France in ‘game of chicken’ with EU on Russia sanctions, as clock ticks to expiry deadline
item.description: The talks will resume on Monday, but the EU-27 agreed there would be no more deadline extensions. "It's turned into a game of chicken [with France]," an EU diplomat said.

item.title: [DW] Canada and EU: A look at the bloc's special relationships
item.description: Though Canada may be some distance from Europe geographically, closer political ties are in the cards. With talk of an associate membership, DW takes a look at other arrangements the EU has with particular countries.

item.title: [EU Observer] Beijing tells EU to weaken ‘Made in Europe’ industrial bill ahead of October showdown
item.description: Beijing and Brussels have made demands and counter-demands as talks on their myriad trade disputes hot up. But they could be derailed by a US-China summit in Washington next week.

item.title: [EU Observer] Polish leader Tusk exposes classified figures on sky-high Ukrainian casualties (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,667)
item.description: With tens of thousands of Ukrainians reportedly killed or wounded each month, the coming autumn and winter campaign could stretch Ukraine’s manpower, air defences, and battered cities to breaking point.

item.title: [EU Observer] Scene set for verbal punch-up at UN in New York, as Trump and Netanyahu face critics from EU and further afield
item.description: Brazilian leader Lula da Silva will give the opening speech at the UN in New York on Tuesday morning, in which he will "personally" warn Donald Trump not to interfere in Brazilian elections, before Trump takes the floor.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU commits €3.3bn to Ukrainian drones as funding gap remains unresolved ahead of ‘tough winter’
item.description: As von der Leyen rushes through billions in new funding for Ukrainian drones, EU diplomats are privately questioning Kyiv’s spiralling deficit, while Belgium continues to block the use of frozen Russian assets — intensifying pressure on Europe to find a way to plug Ukraine’s widening funding gap.

item.title: [EU Observer] Berlin election shows how the EU turns its most mobile citizens into second‑class voters
item.description: European law gives EU citizens the right to vote in municipal elections, but this does not extend to state or national elections, for which Germany reserves voting rights to German citizens. This results in an odd discrepancy even within a single member state.

item.title: [EU Observer] Sweden begins shipping off prisoners to rented Estonian cells
item.description: While Estonia has prison cells to spare, Sweden's prisons are full. Stockholm will pay €30.6m annually for the first 300 prisoners it sends to a Tartu prison. The deal has been criticised by both countries.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: How does the EU plan to ban social media for under-15s?
item.description: The EU Kids Act promises to wean children off endless scrolling and late‑night gaming, but privacy advocates and parts of the tech industry warn the EU’s own age‑verification system could open the door to new risks.
